CAPN3_c.550del is grounded in a real ClinVar entry (coordinates not independently verified — see notes); all other cases are synthetic, constructed to exercise specific combining-rule paths and, from Milestone 4 on, case-level trans/cis/hemizygous interpretation. specification.version: ClinGen LGMD VCEP Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Guidelines for CAPN3, v2.0 (2025-07-09; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21434844)

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (Variation ID 17621), reported Pathogenic. Known founder mutation, reported to account for up to ~75% of abnormal CAPN3 alleles in some European (esp. Northern Spanish / Basque and other Southern/Western European) populations — this is why ancestry_specific_max_af is meaningfully higher than overall_af rather than roughly equal. PM2 (absent/extremely low frequency) is written up here as MET in the golden case using the low overall AF (0.023%), but a curator reviewing this case should not treat that as settled: PM2 is defined around population rarity, and a founder allele that is locally common in the tested individual's ancestry group is a weaker fit for 'extremely low frequency' than the global AF alone suggests. This is exactly the ancestry-stratification nuance the ACMG Engine Detailed Design Guide flags for PM2 (Section 7, 'Population frequency thresholds'); a real evaluator should key its threshold check off ancestry_specific_max_af, not overall_af, once ancestry is known. Flagged for manual review in the golden case rather than silently trusted. Exact GRCh38 coordinates were not independently verified during curation (see variant.coordinate_verified=false); HGVS (c.550del) and the ClinVar accession are used as the authoritative identifiers instead.

gene_disease_context.disease: Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy, type R1 calpain3-related (LGMDR1 / calpainopathy)

specification.version: ClinGen LGMD VCEP Specifications to the ACMG/AMP Guidelines for CAPN3, v2.0 (2025-07-09; DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21434844)

cases.notes: Real, recurrent CAPN3 missense variant (p.Asp753Asn, ClinVar VCV000281081.42, rs146923842, ClinGen CAID CA7511784), reported in multiple LGMD cohorts (e.g. an 8-patient Italian multicenter series) with real, documented, and now well-sourced controversy. Coordinates (GRCh38 chr15:42410660 G>A, canonical SPDI NC_000015.10:42410659:G:A) confirmed directly from the primary ClinVar VCV page in batch 10, upgrading coordinate_verified from false to true. PRIMARY-SOURCE-CONFIRMED VCEP classification (batch 8 had this secondhand from a web search summary; batch 10 fetched the primary ClinVar page directly and confirmed it verbatim): the ClinGen LGMD VCEP's official 3-star 'reviewed by expert panel' record (SCV007328786.1, evaluated 2025-10-28, erepo.clinicalgenome.org/evrepo/ui/interpretation/8afff73c-4e6c-4e68-9e24-e2192b0159d4) classifies this variant LIKELY BENIGN for autosomal recessive LGMD, via BS1 + BP2. Their exact stated rationale: gnomAD v4.1.0 Grpmax filtering allele frequency 0.002457 (lower 95% CI bound of 22/6060 Middle Eastern chromosomes, including 2 homozygotes) clears their BS1 threshold (>0.001); PM3/PP4 not met (several reported carriers had a second CAPN3 variant that could independently explain their phenotype); one individual's variant was confirmed in cis with a pathogenic variant (c.1401_1403del p.(Glu467del), PMID 38391941) -- BP2; REVEL 0.649, below their PP3 threshold (>=0.70). This project's engine reaches PM2 NOT_MET, BS1 MET (Strong, matching the VCEP), PP3/BP4 both NOT_MET (REVEL genuinely INDETERMINATE by the calibrated-score model used here), landing on VUS -- it cannot reproduce the VCEP's LIKELY_BENIGN call because BP2 (in trans/cis with a pathogenic variant) is not implemented at all, and BS1 alone is Table-5-insufficient for LIKELY_BENIGN without a Supporting-benign criterion alongside it. NEW IN BATCH 10 -- a genuinely opposing real-world signal, not just an unimplemented criterion: a peer-reviewed paper published one month after the VCEP's own evaluation (Bruno et al., 'Recurrent CAPN3 p.Asp753Asn Variant Supports a Potential Dominant Calpainopathy with Variable Clinical Expressivity', Int J Mol Sci 2025;26(23):11384, PMID 41373542, DOI 10.3390/ijms262311384) reports a retrospective multicenter Italian cohort (ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05956132) of 59 patients heterozygous for CAPN3 variants, in which p.Asp753Asn was the single most frequent variant found (8 of 59 patients, 13.5%), all heterozygous with NO second CAPN3 variant identified. These 8 patients (aged 6-80) showed a real, if heterogeneous, phenotypic spectrum -- from asymptomatic hyperCKemia to progressive proximal weakness with contractures and axial involvement -- and new structural modeling proposes a specific mechanism (loss of a stabilizing Asp753-Lys517 salt bridge, disrupting inter-domain coupling) consistent with a dominant-negative effect. The paper's own conclusion: 'the aggregated evidence supports a pathogenic role for p.Asp753Asn' -- for a DIFFERENT disease model than the one the VCEP evaluated. The VCEP's Likely Benign call is explicitly scoped to 'autosomal recessive limb girdle muscular dystrophy' (per its own classification comment); this paper is arguing for pathogenicity in autosomal DOMINANT calpainopathy (LGMDD4), a distinct, less common inheritance model for the same gene that the VCEP specification does not appear to address for this variant. These two real, contemporaneous, credentialed sources are not actually contradicting each other on the facts (both cite essentially the same gnomAD frequency and the same REVEL score) -- they are answering different questions (is this pathogenic FOR RECESSIVE disease vs. is this pathogenic FOR DOMINANT disease) that this project's one-inheritance-pattern-per-gene design (gene_disease_context.yaml fixes CAPN3 as AUTOSOMAL_RECESSIVE, full stop) cannot represent at all -- not a gap in any single evaluator, but a gap in the schema itself, previously only mentioned here in passing (batch 8) as a forward-looking note and now fully primary-source-documented. This project's VUS result is, in that light, arguably the most defensible of the three outcomes on offer (VCEP Likely Benign for recessive disease; this paper's suggestive Pathogenic-leaning case for dominant disease; this project's VUS) precisely because it commits to neither disease model and flags the ambiguity instead -- though that is a fortunate byproduct of missing criteria, not a deliberate design strength.

Individual in-silico tools (SIFT: Tolerated, PolyPhen-2: Benign, Align-GVGD: Class C0) all lean benign, and the substituted residue is conserved as leucine in other mammals -- but deliberately NOT converted into a ComputationalEvidence record here: this project's PP3/BP4 model expects a single calibrated ensemble score (e.g. REVEL), not raw individual-tool outputs stacked together, which is exactly the kind of multi-tool-vote pattern the design guide warns against (see computational_evidence.py docstring). cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (VCV001453744 / RCV002002571), reported Pathogenic (last evaluated 2023-10-06, criteria provided/single submitter). Coordinates independently confirmed via NCBI eutils esummary (canonical_spdi NC_000015.10:42359805:A:G), not just taken from a search snippet. gnomAD reported two slightly different exome AF figures in the ClinVar record (0.00001 and 0.00000, likely different gnomAD releases/subsets aggregated by ClinVar); the higher, more conservative value is used here. Real ClinGen LGMD VCEP CAPN3 PVS1 flowchart likely does resolve this branch; this project's PVS1 evaluator does not implement that flowchart.

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (VCV000468648 / ClinGen Allele Registry CA7511744), classified Pathogenic by the ClinGen LGMD VCEP itself (Evidence Repository record 7f534c0d-0dbe-4d2e-88e2-88c804cde635, approved 2025-04-22): erepo.clinicalgenome.org/evrepo/ui/interpretation/7f534c0d-0dbe-4d2e-88e2-88c804cde635. This is the project's first fixture sourced directly from an official VCEP expert curation record, not just a ClinVar aggregate classification -- and the first REAL calibrated computational (REVEL) score used anywhere in this project (closing a gap open since Milestone 1): REVEL=0.966, well above the real VCEP's own PP3 threshold (>=0.70). Population data: gnomAD v2.1.1 total AF 0.000148 (42/282854, all populations); gnomAD v4.1.0 exomes East Asian filtering allele frequency 0.001250-0.001929 (95% CI bounds, 62/39700 East Asian chromosomes) -- used here as ancestry_specific_max_af (upper bound, consistent with the FAF convention already used for PM2/BA1/BS1 in this project). NOTABLE: the real VCEP's own curation explicitly found this variant's East Asian FAF (0.001929) technically crosses their BS1 threshold (>0.001), but chose NOT to apply BS1 -- an explicit 'BS1 exception' -- because this is one of the most commonly reported CAPN3 variants in East Asian LGMD patients (i.e. a real, expert-judged founder-pathogenic-variant scenario, not a benign-common-variant one). This project's BS1 evaluator cannot make that judgment call (it has no access to case-count/segregation context), but it does correctly decline to auto-resolve: with overall_af below the BS1 threshold but ancestry_specific_max_af crossing it, the evaluator's existing founder-enrichment branch returns MANUAL_REVIEW rather than silently applying BS1 -- landing on exactly the same 'a human needs to look at this' conclusion the real VCEP reached, for the same underlying reason, without knowing why. The real variant's actual Pathogenic classification rests almost entirely on criteria this project's 6-criterion engine does not implement at all (PM3_Strong: observed in trans with a pathogenic variant across multiple case reports; PP1_Strong: segregation in 6 affected relatives across 4 families; PP4: phenotype + reduced calpain-3 protein expression) -- PM2 is explicitly NOT_MET in the real curation too (too common in East Asian populations for PM2_Supporting's <0.0001 threshold), and PP3 (REVEL) is the ONLY real criterion this project's engine and the real VCEP curation share. This fixture is included specifically to show, honestly, how much of a real clinical classification depends on case-level and segregation evidence entirely outside a variant-only automated engine's reach.

population_evidence.source_version: unspecified (per ClinVar submitter note: 'not present in population databases, ExAC no frequency')

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (RCV000379611.3, current record 299395779), reported Pathogenic by Invitae (Sherloc method, 1-star 'criteria provided, single submitter' review status, last evaluated 2017-07-31), canonical splice donor variant disrupting intron 2 of DMD. Coordinates independently confirmed directly from the ClinVar RCV page (GRCh38 chrX:33020138 C>T; DMD is on the minus strand, so this genomic C>T is the transcript-level c.93+1G>A). Reported absent from population databases (ExAC) in the submitter's own description; no gnomAD-specific frequency was stated in the available record, so ExAC is recorded as the source here rather than assumed to be gnomAD. This is the project's second real (non-synthetic) DMD variant, and the first real DMD fixture exercising PVS1's splice-site scope gap (previously only demonstrated on CAPN3, via CAPN3_c.946-1G>A and CAPN3_c.2050+1G>A) -- showing the same evaluator limitation applies identically regardless of gene, since pvs1.py's splice-donor/acceptor handling has no gene-specific logic. With PVS1 returning MANUAL_REVIEW and only PM2 (Moderate, absent from ExAC) MET, the engine lands on VUS, the same story as the CAPN3 splice fixtures, now confirmed on the X-linked gene too.

population_evidence.source_version: genomes (via Ensembl variation endpoint, rs1477369230); cross-confirmed against ClinVar VCV000641807's own reported aggregate gnomAD frequency (0.00006)

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (VCV000641807.15, Variation ID 641807; RCV synonyms RCV000795130, RCV001580547, RCV001830706, RCV002424814, RCV003489872), dbSNP rs1477369230, classified Uncertain significance (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 4 of 6 submissions contributing: GeneDx, Labcorp Genetics/Invitae, Women's Health and Genetics/LabCorp, Ambry Genetics). Coordinates and HGVS independently derived and cross-verified before consulting the primary ClinVar record: mapped DMD's MANE Select transcript (ENST00000357033.9, protein ENSP00000354923) residue 3681 to GRCh38 chrX:31126645-31126647 via the Ensembl REST API, retrieved the codon on both strands (AGA on the coding minus-strand), enumerated all nine possible single-nucleotide substitutions of that codon, and found exactly one produces a stop codon (position 1, coding-strand A>T, i.e. genomic plus-strand T>A at chrX:31126647) -- then confirmed this exact variant is independently cataloged in dbSNP/ClinVar via Ensembl's overlap/variation endpoints, and finally fetched the primary ClinVar VCV page directly, which returned the identical NM_004006.3:c.11041A>T (p.Arg3681Ter) HGVS, confirming the derivation exactly rather than merely being consistent with it. nmd_predicted=false: this is the project's first REAL fixture for PVS1's NMD-escape scope gap (previously only exercised by a hand-built edge-case test, test_pvs1_no_nmd_yields_manual_review_not_a_guess). The variant sits in coding exon 78 of 79, disrupting only the last 5 amino acids of dystrophin's C-terminus -- and every one of the four contributing ClinVar submitters independently states in their own classification comment that NMD is NOT expected here (Invitae: 'not anticipated to result in nonsense mediated decay'; LabCorp: 'nonsense mediated decay is not expected to occur'; Ambry: 'not expected to trigger nonsense-mediated mRNA decay'), so nmd_predicted=false is not this project's own inference -- it is independently corroborated by four separate clinical laboratories applying the standard last-exon/near-final-exon-junction NMD-escape rule. Population data: gnomAD genomes (queried directly via Ensembl's variation endpoint for rs1477369230) shows allele_count=6 out of 110413 total alleles overall (AF=0.0000543), with all 6 observed alleles restricted to the African/African American subpopulation (allele_count=6 of 30322 African alleles, AF=0.000198) -- this precisely matches a peer-reviewed paper's description of this variant as observed in six African individuals in gnomAD v3, and matches ClinVar's own reported aggregate gnomAD frequency (0.00006) to within rounding. Different ClinVar submitters cite different, smaller values from older/other gnomAD releases (Ambry: overall 0.0005%/African 0.007%, i.e. an older ~182k-allele dataset) -- included here for transparency, not smoothed over; rarity conclusions are consistent across all cited datasets even though the exact numbers differ by release. DMD has no published ClinGen VCEP variant-curation specification (confirmed via search this batch -- only a gene-disease-validity curation exists, unrelated to PM2/BS1 thresholds), so this is the first real DMD fixture to expose PM2/BS1's OBSERVED-branch requirement for a configured per-gene threshold; config/population_thresholds.yaml now carries an explicitly-labeled DMD placeholder (0.0001 / 0.001, reusing CAPN3's own pre-batch-4 placeholder values) so this fixture evaluates without guessing at a fabricated 'real' number. With that placeholder, PM2 lands on the same founder-enrichment MANUAL_REVIEW pattern seen in CAPN3_c.550del and CAPN3_c.2120A>G (overall AF below threshold, ancestry-specific AF above it) -- fitting, since the underlying biology (all six copies found in one ancestry group) is exactly that pattern. Combined with PVS1's own MANUAL_REVIEW (NMD-escape scope gap), the engine lands on VUS with manual_review_required=True and no conflicting-evidence flag -- honestly reflecting that two independent, disclosed modeling gaps (not conflicting real evidence) are what's actually blocking a confident automated call here, which matches the real world's own Uncertain significance consensus classification for this variant.

population_evidence.source_version: v2.1/v3.1 (per submitter comments: 'gnomAD no frequency'; also absent from 1000 Genomes and TOPMed)

cases.notes: Real ClinVar entry (VCV000011211.24, Variation ID 11211), classified Pathogenic (criteria provided, multiple submitters, no conflicts; 7 of 8 submissions contributing: Athena Diagnostics, Revvity Omics, Laboratory of Medical Genetics Athens, Eurofins, Labcorp/Invitae, Natera, FRIGE's Institute of Human Genetics, plus a historical 1992 OMIM/literature entry). Nonsense variant in exon 60 of 79, MANE Select transcript. Reported absent from gnomAD (v2.1 and v3.1), 1000 Genomes, and TOPMed by multiple independent submitters -- a cleaner, more unanimous ABSENT call than most fixtures in this set. nmd_predicted=true is a modeling judgment (same convention as DMD_c.2302C>T and CAPN3_c.1939G>T): position 2982 of dystrophin's 3685 aa is in exon 60 of 79, well upstream of the final exon-exon junction, so NMD is expected to degrade the transcript rather than produce a truncated protein. First identified via literature in 1992 (Roberts et al., PMID 1549596) and repeatedly reconfirmed since -- one of the longest continuously-classified-Pathogenic entries in this project's curated set. Added in batch 11 while searching (again unsuccessfully) for a real BP4-MET fixture -- this project still has no real, non-synthetic example of a calibrated computational score landing BENIGN (only CAPN3_c.2257G>A's real INDETERMINATE REVEL score, batch 8); that gap remains open, mirroring the long-standing BA1 gap in being genuinely hard to source from search rather than merely unexamined. This fixture instead grows the curated set with another cleanly-sourced, unsurprising real Pathogenic DMD nonsense variant, adding a second real DMD PVS1-MET example at a different exon/position than DMD_c.2302C>T, without changing the expected result's shape (same LIKELY_PATHOGENIC story: PVS1 Very Strong + PM2 Moderate).

Reviewed by expert panel (ClinGen LGMD VCEP, evaluated 2025-06-24): Pathogenic, via PM3_Very Strong + PP4_Moderate + PM2_Supporting + PM4 (none of which besides PM2/PM4 are implemented by this project). Sourced specifically as batch 14's real fixture for the newly-implemented PM4 evaluator, closing the loop on a variant this project's own notes had referenced by name (in the CAPN3_c.2257G>A enrichment write-up) without ever formally sourcing it. 

repeat_region curation note (the reason this fixture was chosen deliberately, not casually): the official HGVS uses short-tandem-repeat notation, c.1395GGA[2] -- the reference allele is a GGA-trinucleotide run (GGAGGAGGA, 3 copies) and this variant contracts it to 2 copies (GGAGGA), deleting one GGA unit and one glutamate residue. Read naively, that looks exactly like the kind of 'repeat region' PM4 is defined to exclude (Richards et al. 2015: '...in a nonrepeat region'). But the real ClinGen LGMD VCEP's own Pathogenic classification for this exact variant applies PM4 anyway, with no repeat-region caveat or discussion in their comment -- they simply state '...is expected to cause an in-frame deletion of one amino acid, p.(Glu467del) (PM4).' Taken at face value, that is a real, expert-panel-level judgment that a small (2-3 copy) incidental trinucleotide run inside an otherwise unremarkable coding region is not the kind of 'repeat region' the PM4 exclusion is aimed at -- unlike, say, a polyglutamine/polyalanine tract or a locus with a documented high population rate of benign in-frame indels, which is what the exclusion exists to guard against (indels there are common, expected, and usually uninformative; sequencing/alignment artifacts are also more likely). This fixture's repeat_region is therefore curated as false, on the strength of that real-world precedent, not guessed either way. 

protein_length_change_aa is curated as 1 (a single glutamate residue), which is what the VCEP, Invitae/Labcorp, and LabCorp submitter comments all independently confirm ('deletion of 1 amino acid(s)', 'remove one amino acid'). This project's PM4 evaluator downgrades single-residue in-frame changes to Supporting strength by default (the general ClinGen SVI caution, not CAPN3-specific). Worth flagging honestly: the real VCEP's comment states plain 'PM4' with no strength qualifier, unlike their explicitly qualified 'PM3_Very Strong', 'PP4_Moderate', and 'PM2_Supporting' in the same sentence -- which reads as their having applied PM4 at its unmodified default (Moderate), not Supporting. This project's generic Supporting default for this fixture is therefore a disclosed departure from what the real CAPN3-specific VCEP appears to have done, not a hidden one -- consistent with how this project has already handled other real-vs-project strength mismatches (e.g. PM2's Supporting-vs-Moderate story elsewhere in this file). 

Population frequency: gnomAD v4.1.0 exomes (matching the VCEP's own primary source), overall AF 1.437e-05 (21/1,461,872 total alleles), NFE-specific 1.888e-05 (21/1,111,998), both retrieved directly from Ensembl's variation endpoint (dbSNP rs746075428 population frequencies) rather than approximated from the VCEP's filtering-allele-frequency (FAF) statistic, which is a more conservative upper-confidence-bound figure, not a raw allele frequency, and would not be a fair like-for-like match to how this project reports overall_af / ancestry_specific_max_af elsewhere. Both figures sit far below CAPN3's real ClinGen LGMD VCEP thresholds (PM2_Supporting <0.0001; BS1_Strong >0.001; BA1 >0.003). Exact GRCh38 coordinates were not independently re-verified during curation beyond the ClinVar-stated 42401681-42401683 (see variant.coordinate_verified=false, matching this project's existing convention for HGVS/ClinVar-ID-anchored fixtures).

Worth flagging, same pattern as CAPN3_c.1401_1403del: the VCEP's comment states plain 'PM4' with no strength qualifier (unlike their explicitly qualified 'PM3_Very Strong', 'PP4_Strong', and 'PM2_Supporting' in the same sentence), reading as their default (Moderate) strength -- which for a 5-residue deletion is also exactly what this project's evaluator independently lands on (no single-residue downgrade applies here), so this fixture's PM4 strength matches the real VCEP's, unlike the single-residue one.
